market_summary: The pre-market setup is constructive but selective, based on 1595 articles from Yahoo Finance, Investing.com, TradingView, The Motley Fool, 24/7 Wall St.. The dominant theme is macro, with 654 macro items, 529 company items, 366 industry items, and 46 policy items. The tape looks more useful for identifying near-term rotation and risk appetite than for making a single directional index call.
macro_summary: Late Cycle Markets are balancing easier policy expectations against growth and earnings risk, keeping leadership narrow and confirmation dependent. The market is taking its direction from Fed/rates, with investors testing whether policy support can offset slower growth and earnings risk. Macro coverage is concentrated around Fed/rates (189), oil/energy (105), inflation (91), growth/jobs (22). The practical implication is that equity rallies may need confirmation from rates and inflation expectations; if yields rise while growth headlines weaken, risk appetite can fade quickly.
risk_summary: Sentiment is constructive but selective: 230 positive, 143 negative, and 1222 neutral articles. My read is to avoid treating headline volume as conviction by itself; the more important signal is whether macro-sensitive and technology-sensitive stories are pointing in the same direction.
